values.value: • Use the clean path to close faster and more confidently. • Confirm that no hidden dependencies such as budget release, policy clearance, committee approval, or IT check remain. • Sequence next steps tightly because dependency-free deals can move well when managed actively. • Do not create delay through internal slow follow-up on your side. • Convert simplicity into momentum.
16|No dependency
Buyer may say, 'Nothing major is pending.' Response: 'That is excellent. Then we can move faster by locking the remaining actions and dates now.'
Good. Keep the close plan simple and move quickly while there are fewer moving parts.
Low risk. Push speed.
Ask: 'Since there are no major dependencies, can we lock the next two decision steps now?'
No dependency

• Clarify the dependency and keep it visible without letting it control the deal. • Ask who owns that dependency and when it is expected to clear. • Build follow-up around the dependency date. • Work in parallel on everything else that can be completed now. • Reduce the chance of a small dependency becoming a big excuse.
16|Yes, but insignificant
Buyer may say, 'There is a small dependency.' Response: 'Fine. Let us make it visible and work around everything else in parallel.'
Name the dependency clearly and keep it on a watchlist. Small blockers become big surprises when ignored.
Risk: Small dependency can still delay closure.
Ask: 'What exactly is the dependency, and by when will it be resolved?'
Yes, but insignificant

• Treat this as a major risk to forecast and closure timing. • Understand exactly what event must happen, who controls it, and how likely it is. • Check whether your deal can be structured in phases to reduce dependency pressure. • Keep leadership informed internally if this is a strategic opportunity. • Do not forecast aggressively until the dependency has a clear path.
16|Yes, significant
Buyer may say, 'This depends on another decision first.' Response: 'Understood. Then I want to plan this around that reality rather than over-forecast the close.'
Do not ignore this. Build the deal plan around the dependency owner, date, and workaround path.
High risk: External or internal blocker present.
Ask: 'What must happen first, who controls it, and is there any way to parallel-track our work?'
Yes, significant

• Find out what external or internal event the decision depends on before you rely on the timeline. • Ask about budget release, approvals, academic cycle, leadership sign-off, procurement event, or other linked decisions. • Make hidden dependencies visible now, not late in the cycle. • This will improve both forecasting and next-step planning. • Deals often slip because this question was never asked properly.
16|Don't know
Buyer may say, 'I am not sure what else this depends on.' Response: 'No problem. Let us map the possible approvals and linked events now so we do not get surprised later.'
Surface the hidden blockers now. Unseen dependencies are one of the easiest ways for a 'good' deal to slip.
High risk: Unknown blocker risk.
Ask: 'Is this dependent on budget release, leadership approval, vendor onboarding, or another project?'
Don't know
Are there any dependency risk? Is the decision dependent on any event/situation to happen?
